python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_resident_ordered_flag returns None for FAST parallel_groves, making the OFF define bypass ordered traversal in the common experiment route
Explicit public inference_engine=sequential can still force ordered traversal, but that is a separate route-specific experiment rather than a P01/P03 combination
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Paired ordered forest output traversal
affected_estimators: tree wrappers selecting ordered forest inference
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Two row/output items share the tree loop, with independent ordered accumulators and a guarded second plane.
limitations: Requires ordered inference, not parallel_groves.
Does not change traversal representation or node thresholds.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: The public resident OFF prerequisite selects _launch_grove_lanes; forest_grove32_kernel and forest_vector_grove32_kernel allocate the selected capacity and stage rows before their unchanged traversals when feature bytes fit
source_evidence: python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_resident_ordered_flag lets FAST parallel_groves accept that compiled False
core/forest_inference.mojo:launch_forest_inference[GROVE=True] selects _launch_grove_lanes unless the existing row-thread override applies
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Forest shared rows with a two KiB block budget
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Enable shared-row staging with capacity derived from 2048 bytes divided by Float32 size and groves per block; overflow rows use direct loads.
prerequisites: MOJOLEARN_FOREST_ORDERED_RESIDENT_OFF in both arms for public FAST resident callers
Public inference_engine auto or parallel_groves; no forced row-thread schedule
limitations: Extends existing staging code with a different storage budget; existing 256-feature staging outcome is not claimed as new evidence.
With P01, per-row capacity increases because fewer rows share the same fixed byte budget.
Scalar-output staging is applicable only to one-output leaves; vector leaves have the existing capacity dispatch.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: _predict_forest_labels calls forest_predict_resident_labels_gpu_binding, then resident_predict_labels and ResidentForest's label methods; launch_forest_argmax and forest_argmax_kernel share AFT_ARGMAX_ROWS for complete class-code output coverage
source_evidence: python/mojolearn/_forest_protocol.py:_predict_forest_labels returns None unless effective mode is fast and _prediction_engine() is parallel_groves; FAST auto resolves to that name
core/forest_inference_model.mojo:ResidentForest label paths call launch_forest_argmax after either ordered or grove traversal, so the default ordered resident policy does not bypass P04
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Paired row forest class argmax
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Two row planes per worker call a shared first-max helper; nonfinite sentinel and class order remain unchanged.
limitations: No effect for regression or raw/probability requests that do not consume class codes.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: gbdt_resident_predict_binding reaches _predict_device; GBDT_PREDICT_PACKED with a nonempty oblivious model selects _apply_all. Its grid covers 512 rows/block under P05, matching two 256-lane planes in compute_bins_and_add_all_kernel and its doubled grid stride
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Two rows reuse packed GBDT split descriptors
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Each worker loads a tree/split descriptor once for two independent rows; the grid and stride account for two row planes.
prerequisites: MOJOLEARN_GBDT_PREDICT_PACKED
limitations: Prerequisite is held equal in both arms; no packed-prediction default is changed.
Non-symmetric fallback keeps its original kernel.
Packed path preparation and its synchronization remain in the future cold-use timed boundary.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: Both gbdt/resident_model.mojo and gbdt/train.mojo import LINK_BLOCK and use it in grid construction and resident_link_kernel block_dim; the kernel derives its index/stride from actual block_dim/grid_dim
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Smaller GBDT resident link block
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: LINK_BLOCK is 128 rather than 256; the existing grid-stride kernel and its callers share the constant.
limitations: Same software binary64 exp/div; this is a scheduling experiment, not reduced precision.
Standalone users of the shared resident-link constant are also affected and need future coverage.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: tree_shap_values computes row_units=n_trees*ceil(rc/SHAP_ROW_TILE) for each chunk and uses it for every direct/table/decision-table row launch; each kernel reverses that mapping to the same tree*rc+row unit before calling the original unit implementation
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: TreeSHAP four-row tree tiles
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Four adjacent rows per tree worker in direct, leaf-table and decision-table paths, with exact row-tail guards.
limitations: Mutually exclusive with MOJOLEARN_SHAP_FAST_ROW_PAIR.
Existing pair audit counter is not used to claim quartet execution.
Sequential unit calls change work mapping; no new persistent model cache is claimed.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: shap_prepare, _Forest preparation and tree_shap_values launches use TPB and _grid; kernel _uid or explicit indexing uses that same TPB, including P07/P10 combinations
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: TreeSHAP smaller worker block
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: TPB is 64 rather than 128 for SHAP preparation, table, row and fold kernels.
limitations: Requires full preparation-plus-explanation coverage, not only the row kernel.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: tree_shap_values uses _rows_per_chunk(BUF_BYTES) for its contribution allocation and per-iteration rc; it launches and folds every rc-row chunk before advancing r0 by rc
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: TreeSHAP contribution scratch budget
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Contribution scratch budget becomes 64 MiB instead of 128 MiB, with unchanged per-tree units cap and complete row coverage.
limitations: Can increase chunk count and lose performance; no win claimed.
The full output and leaf table allocations retain existing sizes, so this is not a bound on total GPU memory.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: tree_shap_values launches fold_kernel with ceil(fu/AFT_SHAP_FOLD_ITEMS) logical workers; fold_kernel uses TPB*AFT_SHAP_FOLD_ITEMS for each block base and invokes shap_fold_unit for both guarded output-cell planes
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Paired TreeSHAP output-cell folding
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Two independent flattened attribution output cells per worker; each still folds every original tree contribution in the original order.
limitations: Refines initial row-tiling idea to output-cell tiling matching the existing fold layout.
No cross-cell reduction or discarded feature attribution.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: dart_step launches dart_row_kernel for n rows and dart_predict launches dart_predict_kernel for k*n class/row cells; both callers divide logical work by AFT_DART_ROWS and kernels multiply block bases and capped-grid strides by the same factor
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Paired DART residual and prediction scheduling
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Two contiguous lane planes per worker in dart_row_kernel and dart_predict_kernel; launch grids and grid strides use the same tile.
limitations: Dropout draws and unit functions are unchanged.
For prediction a work unit is a class/row cell, not always an entire multiclass row.

experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.caller_integration: dart_add performs existing apply/leaf-sum/Newton work, then launches dart_add_kernel with ceil(n/AFT_DART_ADD_ROWS) logical workers; the kernel applies the original dart_add_unit to the same two row planes and uses a matching multiplied grid stride
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.title: Paired DART score addition scheduling
experiments/apple_fast_trees/P.json.mechanism: Two row planes per worker in dart_add_kernel, preserving factor, shrinkage and leaf lookup in the existing unit.
limitations: Does not fuse Newton reduction with score addition or change normalization.
